defect.description: A NETRC path is still expanded under the home directory: os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}") turns NETRC=/etc/ci/netrc into a path like /home/user//etc/ci/netrc, so a NETRC file outside the home directory (an absolute path, or one starting with ~) is never found and no credentials are returned; only the default NETRC_FILES names should get the ~/ prefix.

review_items: Absolute NETRC paths mangled by unconditional ~/ prefix in expanduser (line 17)
Empty NETRC string not treated as unset, resolves to home directory
NETRC treated as filename inside ~/ rather than full path; skip prefix for NETRC
Test only covers relative NETRC path; add absolute path test
votes.evidence_quote: Line 17 constructs `f"~/{name}"` → `~/etc/custom_netrc`, and `expanduser` turns that into `/Users/msobroza//etc/custom_netrc`, which doesn't exist. The function returns `None` instead of reading the intended file.
votes.justification: The review's first finding names the unconditional ~/ prefix in the expanduser call. It says this breaks absolute NETRC paths so no credentials are returned, which is the known defect. Later findings on tilde values and NETRC as a full path also cover it.
